messages:
Maya R: heads up — trying to sketch the console flow for automatic fallback handoffs. want to avoid surprises for SREs and product. thoughts?

Trent L: +1. main UX questions: how explicit is the handoff in the console? do we force a confirmation when it triggers or just surface an audit event? :thinking_face:

Ash (ops): prefer audit-first. automatic handoff should show a toast + timeline entry, but not block traffic. human confirmation feels risky for P0 incidents.

Micah (product): agree audit-first. product wants a quick way to "replay" the decision so PMs can see why a request routed to fallback. maybe a small "explain" panel next to the route history.

Trent L: what about severity-based prompts? e.g., for high-impact customers we can surface a modal asking ops to accept fallback for the first n occurrences.

Maya R: that matches earlier convo but adds complexity. would require customer tier metadata tied to policy. also increases rollout friction.

Ash (ops): can we instead have a two-tier behavior: auto-fallback ON by default, and an optional "require approval on first failover within X minutes" toggle per rollout? keeps default simple but enables guardrails.

Micah (product): yes — UI could show a small badge on the rollout card: "Approval: first-fail (optional)". clicking expands explanation + button to toggle.

Kai: quick implementation question: what payload do we include in the audit event to make the playback useful? need model variant, request id, trigger reason, latency, error code, and KV-cache state snapshot? :eyes:

Trent L: minimal useful set: request_id, route_policy_id, trigger_type (eg 502, token_limit, latency_sla), model_variant_from, model_variant_to, timestamp, sample_input_hash. keep KV snapshot optional because it's heavy.

Maya R: +1. also include a compact trace link that opens the full trace in the observability tab. playback UI can show a timeline and a diff between outputs if available.

Ash (ops): important: retention policy. we can't store full request payloads forever. recommend 90 days for full playback data and 1 year for metadata-only events. ops/legal ok with that?

Micah (product): 90 days full / 365 metadata seems reasonable. add a "download audit bundle" button for enterprise customers with longer retention plans.

Trent L: UX for the console: rollout detail page should have a "Fallback events" stream with filters: severity, trigger_type, customer_tier, time window, and a "simulate" button that replays the routing decision against a saved sample input.

Maya R: simulate is great but needs guardrails — simulate must be sandboxed and not counted as production tokens. show a clear red banner when in simulate mode.

Kai: for simulate we'll reuse the eval infra. proto for simulation call: 
```
POST /internal/simulate-routing
{
  "route_policy_id": "rp_123",
  "sample_input_hash": "sha256:...",
  "simulate_time": "now",
  "include_kv_cache": false
}
```
Response includes chosen path and reason.

Trent L: we should also add a small metric in the rollout header: "fallback-rate (1h/24h)" and a tiny sparkline. ops can click to see correlated infra signals.

Ash (ops): final ops ask: in the audit event include the autoscale snapshot (pool sizes) so we can correlate capacity pressure to fallback spikes. something lightweight: gpu_count, queued_reqs, avg_inflight.

Maya R: agreed. I'll draft the console mockups and a minimal audit schema. will drop in the design channel later.

deploy-bot: policy rp_123 updated by Maya R (draft) — staging deploy queued :gear:

Micah (product): awesome, thanks Maya. follow-up: can we add a checkbox "Notify customers on fallback" for public APIs? legal might want opt-in.

Ash (ops): adding customer notifications requires integration with our notifications service. doable but separate PR. for now toggle can just set a flag on the policy.

Maya R: noted. I'll include the flag in the mock and in the audit schema: notify_customers: true|false.

Trent L: this is shaping up. next steps: Maya to post mocks + schema, engineering to review and estimate. we should keep the initial MVP conservative — audit-first, simulate, sparkline, 90/365 retention.

Maya R: thanks all — will post by EOD and tag you. :thumbsup:
